page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with marginal references in the right margin, and a signature at the foot.

main_text.p: & cuius nũntium lætificare debet insulas multas, regnum esse Christi, non Patris præcisè, verborum illorum, ꝟ. 3. Ignis ante ipsum precedet, & inflammabit in circuitu inimicos eius, nonne egregius est commentarius id quod dicit Apostolus 2. Thess. 7. In revelatione Domini Iesu de coelo cum angelis virtutis eius in flamma ignis, dantis vindictam iis, qui non noverunt Deum? Verba etiam illa ꝟ. 4. vidit & commota est terra, & ꝟ. 5. Montes sicut cera fluxerunt a facie Domini, a facie Domini omnis terra. Et ꝟ. 6. viderunt omnes populi gloriam eius, eum sine dubio significant, qui venit vel venturus est, qui se videndum omnibus populis exhibuit vel exhibiturus est. Quis autem ille est? Pater, an Filius? certè Filius potius quàm Pater. Addit ꝟ. 7. Confundantur omnes qui adorant sculptilia, &c. Quis suo aduentu, & ut loquitur Apostolus, τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ [?] omnes idololatras confundet, nisi Christus? ꝟ. 10. Valde exaltatus es super omnes Deos, hoc est, angelos, de utro convenientius id dicitur, de Patre, an de Filio? exaltatio super angelos de Filio prædicari solet ab Apostolis, de Patre non item. Denique inde propheta ansam arripit hortandi pios ad odium mali; quoniam, quamvis in hoc seculo floreant impij, affligantur autem pij, tamen in aduentu illo Domini bene erit pijs, liberabuntur ab impijs, & sempiterni gaudij messem amplam referent, hoc quidem tempore jam sati, sed adhuc, vel latentis in terra, vel saltem fructum suum nondum edentis id quod nullius alius aduentu fiet, quam unius Domini nostri Iesu Christi, cui sit gloria in æternum, Amen.

page.notes: Right margin references, read from the scan: "2. Thess" and "2. 8." beside the "Confundantur" line, "Eph. 1." and "21." beside "uenientius", and "Heb. 1." and "&c." beside "Denique"; they are written as single notes below, placed approximately. The Greek phrase at ꝟ. 7 is faint; the final word is doubtful (possibly αὐτοῦ or αὐτῆ). The signature "S 2" at the foot is doubtful. A small mark "c" lies below the text at the centre; it is a printer's mark, not transcribed. No catchword is visible. Paragraph division is uncertain: the text shows no clear indents, so it is treated as one paragraph. The Latin ꝟ marks are transcribed as V. with stops as printed.
